title: How to organise the medicine cabinet or wall storage
description:
To hold the medicine and first aid you would need tonight, and nothing you stopped needing years ago.

This is the Medicine Cabinet or Wall Storage in the Primary Bathroom. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Three labeled bins, pain relief, stomach and cold, first aid, each holding only in-date items. Prescriptions grouped by the name on the label, the first aid bin small enough to carry one-handed to whoever is bleeding, and the whole cabinet above a child's reach with a catch on it if children are in the house.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Read every label and every date, including the small print on the boxes you kept because the box was still goo
Straighten: Group by the reason you come to this cabinet: headache, stomach, cut, cold, eyes.
Shine: Take the shelves out and wash off the sticky rings left by cough syrup and the dust of old blister foil.
Safety: Bathroom humidity breaks tablets and capsules down faster than a bedroom shelf does, so move anything you take
Standardize: Bins are labeled by symptom rather than brand, so a guest or a sitter can find what they need without asking w
Sustain: Every time you come home from the pharmacy, the new box goes into its bin and you read the dates of everything

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Only in-date, correctly labeled, currently needed medicine lives here, grouped by symptom and kept above child reach.
